metadata.title: Warehouse Management & Fulfilment Platform Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: How Picqer must change when channels and carriers change, labour is scarce, peak volumes spike, traceability rules tighten, Katapull integrates its hub, or mechanisation becomes mainstream.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: A single-tenant stock list per webshop with hard-coded imports from one store, printed picklists, labels from carrier portals and stock counted once a year; 3PL clients get Excel exports.
metadata.residualArchitecture: A multi-tenant warehouse core with an append-only stock ledger, location model and lot tracking; adapters for stores, carriers, hub siblings and hardware behind stable internal contracts; an event stream feeding webhooks, reports and billing; rules as data; and the same workflows exposed in web, app and client portal.

stressors.name: A major webshop platform, marketplace or carrier changes its API or terms at short notice
stressors.detection: Failed imports or label calls in monitoring, partner announcements, support tickets.
stressors.attractor: Orders stop flowing or labels fail during the working day; customers blame the WMS.
stressors.businessReaction: Fix adapters centrally, fall back to another shipping platform via rules, and notify affected accounts.
stressors.residue: Store and carrier specifics live in replaceable adapters; rules can switch shipping method without code.

impacts.effect: Flow continues via retry and fallback.

stressors.name: Warehouse labour becomes scarce and mostly temporary
stressors.detection: Vacancies unfilled, higher temp share, rising error rates of new staff.
stressors.attractor: Warehouses depend on untrained staff; errors and slow peak days follow.
stressors.businessReaction: Make every task guided and scan-verified in the app; let new staff work after minutes of instruction.
stressors.residue: Knowledge sits in the system (locations, routes, rules, packaging advice) instead of in people.

stressors.name: Peak season brings several times normal order volume
stressors.detection: Order backlog and API load in November and December; customer peak plans.
stressors.attractor: Cut-offs missed, systems slow, temp staff overwhelmed.
stressors.businessReaction: Rely on guided temp work, batching, singles and fallback shipping routes; scale cloud capacity.
stressors.residue: Reuses guided work and replaceable adapters; peak becomes a capacity question, not a redesign.

impacts.effect: Reliability at peak is a reference argument.

stressors.name: Retailers and regulators demand batch and expiry traceability for food, supplements and cosmetics
stressors.detection: Fulfilment clients in regulated categories, retailer audits, recall requests.
stressors.attractor: Without lot data, 3PLs lose regulated clients and cannot execute recalls.
stressors.businessReaction: Record batch and best-before at receipt, track through all movements and show in the portal.
stressors.residue: Lot is a first-class dimension of the stock ledger.

stressors.name: Katapull expects Picqer to integrate deeply with Logic4, DeliveryMatch, Returnista, Transus and others
stressors.detection: Group roadmap decisions, Logic4 customers asking for a WMS, co-selling targets.
stressors.attractor: Pressure for exclusive or preferential connections could weaken Picqer's open-platform promise.
stressors.businessReaction: Build hub bridges on the same public API and event contracts that other partners use; keep third-party integrations listed.
stressors.residue: A hub bridge layer on public contracts, not private back doors.

impacts.effect: Open warehouse core of the hub.

stressors.name: Goods-to-person systems and robots become affordable for mid-size warehouses
stressors.detection: Hardware partner pipeline, customers asking for AutoStore or picking robots below enterprise volume.
stressors.attractor: Customers might move to enterprise WMS with warehouse control systems.
stressors.businessReaction: Standardise mechanisation adapters with partners and task hand-over between people and machines.
stressors.residue: Hardware behind adapter contracts; picking tasks are device-agnostic.

stressors.name: Fulfilment companies face margin pressure and must bill every activity
stressors.detection: Rising labour and energy cost, 3PL requests for invoicing, churn to 3PL-specific WMS.
stressors.attractor: Unbilled packaging, storage and returns erode 3PL margins.
stressors.businessReaction: Ship client invoicing on top of recorded activity and packaging usage.
stressors.residue: Every warehouse event is billable data via the activity log.
